birras.bajada: Each bar shows three beers and the rest sit behind a {mas}. Mark yours and those will be the three. You can mark only styles, only brands, or none.

vos.bajada: It's the name you appear with in the public contributors table and under your photos. Your Google name and email aren't shown anywhere.
vos.label: Your username
vos.ayuda: We made one for you from your name. You can change it to whatever you want —it has to be unique, so it may be taken— or delete it and not appear anywhere. You can change it anytime in Settings.

ajustes.bajada: The app starts with these every time you open it. They're the three values people change most, and they're all in Settings if you want to change them later.
ajustes.radioAyuda: How far around you the map and list open.
ajustes.monedaAyuda: The one for bars you add by hand. If you pick the bar from the search, the currency comes from the country. Prices are always shown in the bar's currency: nothing is converted.
ajustes.vasoAyuda: Which size the price keypad starts with. A pint is 473 ml in the US and Argentina, and 568 in the UK.

como.bajada: The only parts of the app you can't figure out by looking at it.

nivel.texto: It comes from the beers you logged in the {fuerte}, not your all-time total. If you stop logging, it drops. That's why it says how you're doing, not how much you've ever piled up.

donde.texto: Saying which bar is optional, but {fuerte}: without a bar there's no way to place them, and that table is by proximity. It's one more tap and it's what puts you in the ranking.
donde.fuerte: beers without a bar don't count toward the who-drank-most-around-here table

nota.titulo: Ratings are for beers, not the bar
nota.texto: You rate each beer by dragging your finger over the stars, in half-point steps. The rating you see on a bar is the average of its beers' ratings — not an opinion about the place, the music or the staff.
